★ LLMjacking honeypot study: AI infrastructure scanned within 3 hours of Shodan indexing, 23% of traffic targeting model capability endpoints

A Raspberry Pi running Ollama/LM Studio/AutoGPT/LangServe/MCP attracted 113K+ requests in a month, with 23% probing AI-specific endpoints (/api/tags, /v1/models, /.well-known/mcp.json) and 175 active hijacking attempts in the final week targeting compute theft and .env credential exfiltration. Shared LLM-Scanner tooling updated mid-experiment to detect honeypots, signalling a maturing attacker ecosystem. Mitigations: bind model servers to localhost, gate remote access with OIDC/OAuth2 short-lived tokens, segment AI infra with allowlists, issue separate tokens per MCP/LLM/RAG component, and SIEM-pipe prompt logs with consumption quotas.

★ Foxconn ransomware attack (Nitrogen gang): 8TB stolen including confidential Apple, Intel, Google, Nvidia documents

The Nitrogen ransomware gang hit Foxconn's North American factories and claims to have exfiltrated 8TB/11M+ documents containing confidential designs and project files from major tech customers. Foxconn confirmed the attack; scope of customer IP exposure is significant for anyone in the NVDA, AAPL, GOOG supply chain.

EntryPoint hijacking: DLL EP overwrite technique avoids thread-creation APIs, extends attacker dwell time

The technique overwrites the EntryPoint of legitimate DLLs (e.g. kernelbase.dll), executing shellcode via thread pools while patching PEB loader structures and restoring the original EP to maintain process stability. PoC tools EPI and LdrShuffle demonstrate viability. Detection requires continuous PEB/LDR scanning, OriginalBase vs DllBase comparison, and correlation of OpenProcess/ReadProcessMemory with suspicious outbound traffic.

SIGINT // daily intelligence brief · Thu 14 May 2026

Open full interactive brief ↗

6 threads · 18 stories · ~9 min read · 15 sources

Artificial intelligence

★ Google launches Gemini Intelligence platform: Googlebooks, agentic Android, AI cursor

Google's Android Show pre-I/O event unveiled Googlebooks (Android-native laptops shipping fall 2026 with Dell/HP/Lenovo/Acer/Asus), a Gemini Intelligence cross-device agentic platform with on-screen context awareness, and a 'Magic Pointer' AI cursor. Gemini will handle in-app agentic task execution, custom widgets, and Chrome auto-browse — delivered via Play Services updates rather than waiting for Android 17. Google is positioning this as a unified AI intelligence layer across hardware, a direct answer to Apple's stalled Siri AI ambitions.

arstechnica.com · mail.beehiiv.com · arstechnica.com ↗

★ GTIG: First criminal AI-developed zero-day used in the wild; PRC actors scale CVE analysis with LLMs

Google's Threat Intelligence Group documented the first observed criminal use of an AI-developed zero-day — a 2FA-bypass exploit against an open-source sysadmin tool, disrupted before deployment. Separately, PRC actors chained persona jailbreaks with a Claude plugin and 85,000 historical bug cases to automate CVE analysis at scale, and Russia-nexus groups are using LLM-generated decoy logic to pad malware payloads and evade static signatures. The PROMPTSPY Android backdoor autonomously interprets on-screen UI and issues actions, signalling a new class of agentic malware.

cloud.google.com · cloud.google.com ↗

Claude Opus 4.7 Fast mode enters research preview; OpenAI publishes self-repairing agent loop cookbook

Anthropic's Fast mode for Claude Opus 4.7 is now opt-in in the API, Claude Code, Cursor, Warp, and Windsurf, with plans to make it the default. OpenAI simultaneously published a Codex cookbook for iterative agent loops that review, repair, and validate their own output — a concrete agentic architecture pattern for production use.

tldr.tech · developers.openai.com ↗

Modal Engineering: AI inference cold-start reduced from kiloseconds to tens of seconds via serverless GPU architecture

Modal published a detailed engineering post on achieving truly serverless GPU inference, cutting replica spin-up time from multiple kiloseconds to tens of seconds. The piece dissects the storage, image caching, and scheduling layers that make variable inference demand tractable without pre-provisioned capacity — directly relevant for anyone building or evaluating inference infrastructure.

modal.com · modal.com ↗

Statewright: State machine guardrails for AI agent tool access improve coding benchmark success rates

Statewright is an open-source framework that constrains which tools an AI coding agent can access based on its current workflow phase (planning, testing, etc.), using deterministic state machines rather than letting the model decide. The narrowed action space measurably increases benchmark success rates and reduces wasted tool calls — a practical architectural pattern for production agentic systems.

github.com · github.com ↗

IAM & cybersecurity

★ Shai-Hulud/TeamPCP supply chain campaign: TanStack 42 npm packages compromised via OIDC token theft from GitHub Actions runner memory

On May 11, TeamPCP used a pull_request_target misconfiguration, GitHub Actions cache poisoning, and live OIDC token extraction from the Runner.Worker process to push 84 malicious versions across 42 @tanstack/* packages. The payload harvested AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Vault, npm, GitHub, and SSH credentials and exfiltrated via Session/Oxen network; a dead-man's switch ('IfYouRevokeThisTokenItWillWipeTheComputerOfTheOwner') triggered destructive actions if the token was revoked before persistence was removed. Defenders must remove launchd/systemd units and Claude Code SessionStart hooks BEFORE rotating tokens, block egress to api.masscan.cloud, and audit pull_request_target workflows.

tanstack.com · cybersecurityreach.org · tanstack.com ↗

★ CheckMarx Jenkins AST plugin backdoored by TeamPCP via unrotated Trivy breach credentials

TeamPCP pivoted from their March Trivy scanner compromise — using credentials Checkmarx never rotated — to push a rogue version (2026.5.09) of the official Checkmarx Jenkins AST plugin to the Jenkins Marketplace on May 9, delivering an infostealer. The malicious build sat outside the release pipeline, lacked a Git tag, and broke the date-based versioning scheme. Roll back to 2.0.13-829.vc72453fa_1c16, rotate all secrets on Jenkins runners that executed the plugin, and treat any vendor breach involving stolen repo credentials as a standing supply-chain risk until rotation is independently confirmed.

tldr.tech · links.tldrnewsletter.com ↗

★ Dirty Frag: Public LPE exploit chains two Linux kernel bugs (CVE-2026-43284, CVE-2026-43500) to root via esp4/esp6 and rxrpc paths

Dirty Frag chains two kernel vulnerabilities in the esp4/esp6 and rxrpc networking subsystems to allow low-privilege users to corrupt page cache data and gain root. Exploit code is already public and has been tested in attacks; Debian, AlmaLinux, and Fedora ship fixes but protection requires patching and rebooting — especially critical on shared servers and VMs. Prioritise patching any multi-tenant Linux infrastructure immediately.

arstechnica.com · arstechnica.com ↗

Instructure pays undisclosed ransom to ShinyHunters after dual Canvas LMS breaches exposing ~275M users

Canvas LMS operator Instructure paid ShinyHunters an undisclosed ransom following two separate breaches that compromised personal data for approximately 275 million users and caused service disruptions. The company received a guarantee the data was destroyed — a guarantee security experts say is unverifiable and that the payment itself incentivises repeat attacks.

insidehighered.com · insidehighered.com ↗

Windows kernel EDR technique: detecting cross-process thread injection with PsSetCreateThreadNotifyRoutine

A detailed walkthrough shows how EDRs use the PsSetCreateThreadNotifyRoutine kernel callback — which fires in the creator's context — to flag cross-process thread creation by comparing PsGetCurrentProcessId() against the notification's ProcessId. The PoC WDF driver logs creator/target PID pairs and filters PID 4 to suppress legitimate kernel threads; production use requires layering in thread start-address inspection (unbacked memory), creator process reputation, and image-load correlation to reduce noise.

tldr.tech

Fintech & fraud

★ US inflation hits 3.8% YoY in April — first time cost of living outpaces wage growth since 2023; rate hike odds rise

April CPI came in at 3.8% year-over-year (up from 3.3% in March and 2.4% in February), driven by energy prices (+18% YoY) and fresh produce, while wage growth slowed to 3.6% — the first real-wage decline in three years. Core CPI remained at 2.8%, well above the Fed's 2% target; traders are now pricing in a rate hike by year-end despite incoming Fed chair Kevin Warsh's general preference for lower rates. Stagflationary pressure is a meaningful headwind for fintech credit and BNPL credit quality.

morningbrew.com

Distributed systems & SWE

★ Databricks high-performance rate limiting: sharded in-memory counters + async batch-reporting cut tail latency 10×

Databricks rebuilt its rate limiter from Redis-backed synchronous checks (10–20ms P99 due to two network hops) to a three-layer architecture: Dicer-routed sharded in-memory counters eliminating Redis, then client-side batch-reporting where clients make zero synchronous calls on the hot path and instead report counts every ~100ms asynchronously. The inversion — the rate limiter is told after decisions rather than consulted before — accepts ~5% overshoot in exchange for ~10× tail latency reduction and predictable server load; token bucket replaced fixed-window counting once the in-memory state layer was stable.

blog.bytebytego.com · databricks.com ↗

Discord replaces manual ScyllaDB scripts with idempotent YAML-defined control plane, cutting multi-day ops to hours

Discord built a Scylla Control Plane using idempotent tasks and YAML-defined workflows to replace fragile manual shell scripts for cluster management. High-stakes database operations that previously took several days now complete in a few hours, with the system designed for safety and repeatability at scale.

discord.com · discord.com ↗

Cloudflare post-mortem: Linux kernel idle-time optimisation caused QUIC CUBIC congestion window death spiral

A Linux kernel optimisation for idle periods inadvertently triggered a QUIC death spiral in Cloudflare's quiche CUBIC implementation: the congestion window got stuck at minimum because idle time was measured from last packet sent rather than last ACK received. Fix: measure idle from the most recent acknowledgement, allowing the controller to distinguish true idleness from congestion — a subtle but critical distinction for any team running QUIC at scale.

blog.cloudflare.com · blog.cloudflare.com ↗

Market intelligence

Google/SpaceX in talks for orbital AI data centres; Project Suncatcher positioned as compute frontier

Google is in active discussions with SpaceX and other launch providers to place data centres in orbit as part of Project Suncatcher, its moonshot for orbital compute. SpaceX is simultaneously pitching orbital data centres to its own investors ahead of a planned IPO. The strategic framing — orbit as a solution to terrestrial data centre land/power constraints — signals that GOOGL and the broader hyperscaler infrastructure build-out is pushing into genuinely new physical frontiers.

techcrunch.com · techcrunch.com ↗

★ Kevin Warsh confirmed as Fed governor; chair vote imminent with inflation data shifting market to rate-hike pricing

The Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh 51-45 as a Fed governor, clearing the path for an imminent chair vote; he is expected to assume the chair role this Friday. With April CPI at 3.8% — well above target — traders have shifted to pricing in a rate hike by year-end, a significant macro reversal with direct implications for growth-stock valuations (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA) and fixed-income positioning.

morningbrew.com

AI semiconductor supply chain: analog/power semis benefiting from AI infrastructure build; TI and NXP raising prices over capacity expansion

The AI infrastructure boom is driving demand for analog and power semiconductors (notably MLCCs), absorbing capacity previously built for EV and solar markets. Texas Instruments and NXP are deliberately avoiding new capacity expansion and instead raising prices to improve margins — a disciplined posture that improves near-term profitability but signals potential supply tightness as AI data centre buildout accelerates.

citriniresearch.com · citriniresearch.com ↗

Sam Altman testifies at OpenAI trial: Musk demanded total control of for-profit arm and succession to his children

Altman took the stand in the OpenAI nonprofit conversion trial, testifying that Musk demanded full control of OpenAI's for-profit arm and rights to pass it to his children — demands Altman called 'hair-raising.' Altman also stated Musk's management style 'demotivated' employees and his departure was a 'morale boost.' The trial's outcome affects OpenAI's ability to complete its for-profit restructuring, with downstream implications for MSFT's $13B+ investment.

6 threads · 16 stories · ~7 min read · 6 sources

Artificial intelligence

★ Thinking Machines Lab 'Interaction Models': Real-Time Multi-Modal AI with Dual-Model Architecture

Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released a research preview of interaction models that ingest voice, video, and text in 200ms streaming chunks — eliminating turn-based latency. A fast foreground model handles real-time presence while an async background model handles reasoning, search, and tool calls. This dual-model split is a direct architectural counter to the agentic-first (long-horizon, async) direction dominating the field.

thinkingmachines.ai · tldrnewsletter.com · thinkingmachines.ai ↗

★ Google Confirms First Known AI-Assisted Zero-Day Discovery and Weaponisation by Criminal Actor

A criminal hacking group used an AI model to discover and weaponise a zero-day in a widely used open-source web admin tool — Google confirmed this is the first documented case of malicious AI-enabled zero-day exploitation. The software vendor was notified in time to patch before broad damage, but the incident signals AI is now lowering the bar for offensive vulnerability research. Directly corroborated by the MCP-based autonomous vuln hunting workflow also covered this cycle.

tldrnewsletter.com · therundownai.com

★ Anthropic Project Glasswing: AI Vuln Discovery Driving Record Patch Volumes Across Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla, Oracle

Anthropic's 'Project Glasswing' AI capability, shared with major vendors, is credited with a dramatic surge in patch volumes: Mozilla fixed 271 Firefox zero-days in one release, Oracle patched 450+ flaws (300+ remotely exploitable unauthenticated), Google fixed 127 Chrome bugs in one update, and Microsoft shipped 118 fixes this Patch Tuesday. This represents a structural shift in the economics of vulnerability discovery — AI is finding bugs faster than humans can ship fixes, compressing patch cycles industry-wide.

krebsonsecurity.com · krebsonsecurity.com ↗

Inference Hardware Split: Cerebras WSE-3 Signals 'Answer Inference' vs 'Agentic Inference' Architectural Divergence

Stratechery argues Cerebras' surging IPO signals a coming bifurcation: 'answer inference' (optimised for token speed, low-latency, voice/wearables) vs 'agentic inference' (optimised for memory hierarchy with large KV caches). The WSE-3 delivers 44GB on-chip SRAM at 21 PB/s — ~6,000× the memory bandwidth of an H100 — but is capacity-constrained for large agentic workloads. Relevant for NVDA positioning and cloud AI infrastructure investment thesis.

AWS published a detailed breakdown of how foundation model scaling has shifted beyond pre-training into post-training and test-time compute, covering the distributed infrastructure required at each stage. Relevant context for AMZN's AI infrastructure positioning and Anthropic partnership economics.

tldrnewsletter.com · huggingface.co ↗

IAM & cybersecurity

★ CVE-2026-41103: Critical Entra ID Credential Impersonation via Forged Credentials — Exploitation Likely

Microsoft May Patch Tuesday includes CVE-2026-41103, a critical EoP that allows an unauthenticated attacker to impersonate any existing user by presenting forged credentials, bypassing Entra ID — Microsoft rates exploitation as 'more likely.' Also notable: CVE-2026-41089, a critical stack-based buffer overflow in Windows Netlogon granting SYSTEM on domain controllers with no privileges or user interaction required. IAM teams should prioritise these patches immediately given the identity-bypass nature of the Entra ID flaw.

krebsonsecurity.com · msrc.microsoft.com ↗

★ CVE-2026-7482: Unauthenticated Heap Dump in Ollama — 300K Exposed Servers at Risk

Cyera disclosed 'Bleeding Llama' (CVE-2026-7482), a critical unauthenticated memory leak in Ollama where an attacker uploads a malformed GGUF file with inflated tensor shape values, triggering out-of-bounds reads via Go's unsafe package that dump the entire process heap. Ollama has 300,000 exposed servers, 170K GitHub stars, and 100M+ Docker pulls — significant exposure for any org running local LLM inference. Patch immediately and block unauthenticated access to Ollama endpoints.

tldrnewsletter.com · cyera.com ↗

★ ScarCruft (APT37) Supply Chain Attack: Trojanised Gaming Platform Deploys BirdCall Backdoor with Android Port

North Korea's ScarCruft compromised sqgame[.]net (a gaming platform targeting ethnic Koreans in China), trojanising its Windows updater and two Android card games to deliver the BirdCall backdoor — the Android variant is new to the group's known arsenal. Android BirdCall uses Zoho WorkDrive over HTTPS for C&C and exfiltrates contacts, SMS, call logs, screenshots, and documents; audio recording is limited to 7–10 PM local time. IOCs: mono.dll SHA-1 95BDB94F6767A3CCE6D92363BBF5BC84B786BDB0; C2 via compromised South Korean domains including 1980food.co[.]kr and lawwell.co[.]kr.

tldrnewsletter.com · welivesecurity.com ↗

A malicious Hugging Face repo impersonating OpenAI's 'Privacy Filter' model reached #1 and amassed 244K downloads before takedown, delivering an infostealer targeting crypto wallets, Discord, and browsers via Windows/macOS/Linux loaders with Defender exclusions and scheduled tasks. Infrastructure links the campaign to Silver Fox operations and the trevlo npm package. A reminder that Hugging Face model cards are an active supply chain attack surface — treat downloaded models as untrusted binaries.

tldrnewsletter.com · thehackernews.com ↗

Operation HookedWing: 4-Year Phishing Campaign Steals 2,000+ Credentials from 500+ Orgs in Critical Infrastructure

A persistent phishing operation used HR/colleague-themed emails linking to GitHub-hosted Outlook-lookalike pages, with loaders customised per victim organisation capturing credentials, IP, and geolocation. Targets span aviation, energy, finance, government, logistics, and tech. GitHub-hosted phishing infrastructure and per-org customisation indicate a sophisticated, semi-automated operation — relevant for fintech AML/fraud teams monitoring account takeover vectors.

★ Figma Data Pipeline Overhaul: CDC + Kafka Reduces Latency from 30+ Hours to <3 Hours, Saves Millions in Replica Costs

Figma replaced daily full-table S3 dumps (taking days for large tables) with a custom CDC pipeline using RDS WAL → Kafka → Snowflake incremental merge, cutting data freshness from 30+ hours to under 3 hours (configurable to minutes). Eliminating dedicated export replicas saved millions annually; billing pipeline runs on 30-minute cycles while other tables default to 3-hour merges. The key engineering detail: CDC stream start offset must precede the snapshot timestamp to avoid a silent 2-hour data gap during bootstrap.

WorkOS shipped Horizon, an agentic code factory where webhooks trigger isolated Cloudflare sandbox agents that plan, code, and verify work end-to-end via a shared context server and orchestrator. Data Warehouse vs Data Lake vs Data Mesh: Trade-offs Summarised

Data warehouses enforce schema-on-write for fast, consistent queries but are slow to onboard new sources. Data lakes store raw everything (schema-on-read) but degrade into unmanageable swamps without strict governance. Data mesh distributes ownership to domain teams with shared standards — effective at scale but demands engineering maturity in every business unit.
